brief: TS Lombard cuts global equities to underweight, including a 3.5pp cut to US equities, because a more hawkish Fed (reaccelerating payrolls, a third straight 0.3% core CPI print, Waller flagging a possible 50bp December hike) combines with a 2027 fiscal drag and peaking hyperscaler capex growth to threaten US EPS growth. It recycles the US proceeds into euro area and India equities, where fading Iran-escalation risk and softer energy prices (Brent below $90, an EIA-flagged crude surplus) support the outlook. Within equities it upgrades Healthcare to strong overweight (pharma-led, M&A, Eli Lilly's weight-loss pill), downgrades Energy to neutral, trims but keeps Taiwan overweight on TSMC's still-strong 43% y/y revenue growth, deepens its China underweight, and moves India to benchmark. It raises credit (+200bp, HY-tilted) and DM govvies (+150bp, periphery-preferred), cuts EM local debt (-6.0pp) and alternatives (-6.0pp, downgrading both precious and industrial metals), and rebuilds cash to 14.0%. In FX it downgrades CHF to -2 and BRL to -1 on Fed/rate-differential risk, and upgrades INR to 0 as fuel prices fall. The portfolio fell 4.95% against a 2.55% benchmark decline, driven by Brazilian local-debt losses and the AI rout.
